title: a request the provider dropped is asked again, and a request the provider refused is not
intent: Three live runs of the wave 41 died the same way and for the same reason: the run of 2026-11-17 16:15 with `Curl failed with exit code 28' after 108 calls of tools, the run of 16:26 with `Curl failed with exit code 16' after 122 calls of tools, and the run of 17:10 with `Curl failed with exit code 28' after 70 calls of tools.  The transport to the provider died, the harness took the death of the transport for the end of the run, and the work of the model — hundreds of calls of tools, a plan read over and over — was thrown away with it.  The request never reached an answer: a provider that drops the connection did not refuse the request, and the run said nothing about that difference.  The wave asks such a request again.  The retry is bounded by a budget of its own (`yeah-turn-default-max-retries'), the journal holds the retry as a record of its own (`retry'), and the model is asked the same question with what the run has done in front of it (wave 47), so the retry continues the work instead of starting it over.  A request that the provider refused is not asked again: a refusal is an answer, and the run fails at once and says why.  The status of the wire decides which of the two it is, and the transport of gptel reports that status as a string (`"529"', `"400"'), so the status is read as a number and not only as a number.  The wave was found by live runs and not by an offline check, and the check that covers it plays the shape of those runs with a fake provider: no network is touched, but the shape is the one that broke the harness, down to the string that carries the status.
objection: The retry repeats the whole request: the transport is given the same question again, and the conversation of the provider starts over with it.  The transcript of the wave 47 puts the work of the run in front of the model, so the model does not have to read the files again, but the tokens of the request are paid for twice, and a provider that is busy for a long time is asked again and again until the budget of the retries is spent.  The budget is small (two by default) and a run that meets a dead provider still ends, where it ended before — the wave buys the runs that meet a provider that dies once and answers the next time, and not the runs that meet a provider that is down.  The wave does not repair the shape of the provider that answers a plan instead of an action (docs/LIVE-EVIDENCE.md): a run that is asked again is asked again by a model that may still only announce its next step.  The wave does not repair the defect of the working directory of a session (`cwd' is still not applied to the tools, docs/PLAN.md 17.1), and it does not repair the shape of the live runs that read the repository and changed nothing (docs/PLAN.md 17.1: the guard that asks the model for the edit after N calls without a change is still open).  The wave does not touch the plan of the owner: the waves 41 to 44 keep their numbers and their order, and the runs that found this defect were the runs of the wave 41.
refuted_by: the run ends when the provider dropped the request; or a request the provider refused is asked again; or the retries of a run are not bounded, or the run ends without saying why it stopped
note: All three controls of the wave were run against the code of this wave and bit; each of them made the check fail by an assertion of the check and not by a crash of Emacs.  The control of `a-dropped-request-is-asked-again' takes the retry out of the harness, and the check fails on twelve assertions: the run does not go on after the dropped request, the model is asked once instead of twice, the retry tells the model nothing, and the retry carries no work of the run.  The control of `a-refused-request-is-not-asked-again' makes every failure retryable, and the check fails on two assertions: the model is asked five times after a refusal, and the journal holds the retry of a request that was refused.  The control of `the-retries-of-a-run-are-bounded' ignores the budget of the retries, and the check fails on four assertions: the model is asked nine times, the journal holds five retries instead of two, the journal holds no error, and the run does not say why it stopped.  The check itself was wrong twice before it was right, and the second of the two defects was a defect of the harness that the check found.  The first version of the fake provider played its script with `pop', which changes the local variable of the caller and not the list itself: the script repeated itself, the harness was asked the same request over and over, and the check measured a harness that never stops -- and the harness under test was a harness that did stop, so the check failed on a harness that worked.  The second version of the fake provider read the status of the wire as a number, which is the shape of no transport: gptel reports the status of the wire as a string (`"529"', `"400"'), so a check that reads a number cannot tell a busy provider from a provider that refused, and in the live harness a refusal of the provider would have been taken for a request that was never answered and asked again.  The wave found the defect in the harness while it was writing the check of the harness, and the check of the wave plays the real shape of the wire down to the string that carries the status.  The retry does not move the machine of the states: the run was waiting for the model and waits again, so the counter of the twenty transitions of `lib/yeah-loop.el' is untouched, and a check that counts the states of a run sees the same states it saw before the wave.  The record of the retry is a record of the journal and not a line of the transcript of the model: the transcript names it in one line (`[retry] the provider dropped the request: ...'), and the journal keeps the reason the retry was made.
